For diabetic patients with high blood pressure and protein in the urine, the American Diabetes Association (ADA) guidelines recommend aiming for a systolic blood pressure target of less than 130 mmHg. The preferred first-line agents among the available options are ACE inhibitors or ARBs. This is particularly beneficial as they can help manage albuminuria.

[ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes, American Diabetes Association, 2024] [MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine), 2024]

results.content: A blood pressure target of <130/80 mmHg is recommended for most adults with diabetes and hypertension. ACE inhibitors or ARBs are preferred first-line agents, particularly in the presence of albuminuria.
results.source: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes
results.citation: Hypertension Management in Diabetes, American Diabetes Association, 2024

results.content: Blood pressure measures the force of blood against artery walls, given as two numbers: systolic (pressure while the heart beats) over diastolic (pressure between beats). A normal reading is below 120/80 mmHg. High blood pressure often has no symptoms, which is why regular checks matter even when feeling fine.
results.citation: Understanding Blood Pressure Readings, MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine), 2024
